title: Naturality for positive finite family
statement: For a positive finite family in the geometric setup, there exist a source comparison eK, a family of target comparisons eC, and a family of derived arrows, satisfying the geometric residue homology equation for every chain representative. Arbitrary comparison equivalences are not prescribed.

proof.text: Take the common source comparison and per-index target comparisons/arrows from the corrected per-index theorem. Choice assembles the target comparisons and arrows into families without changing their representative equations.

statement_change.what: The fixed-equivalence helpers universally prescribed arbitrary additive equivalences. Take a smooth plane cubic over C, S=W=Spec(C), k=id, L=O, n=1, Xi=X and ui=id. A strictly perfect model has one-dimensional degree-one residue homology. Choose the source comparison linearly and the target comparison by composing it with complex conjugation in a coordinate. The identity geometric pullback would force conj(H(phi)(z))=z. Every derived arrow between these affine perfect models has a chain representative (perfect_affine_map_representative), and its residue homology map is C-linear, so this is impossible. Instead choose the comparisons together, with one source comparison shared by all indices. The upper geometric naturality theorem already has precisely this existential quantification, and its statement is unchanged.

old_proof.text: For the empty family there is no positive case; under 0 < n, use the geometric comparison, derived direct-image functoriality, residue pullback, and K-flat comparison for each index to construct the arrows and establish the homology equation.
